newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - B.A.T strangle fires up options.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - B.A.T strangle fires up options.

text.p: The UK traded options market saw some speculators return on Wednesday after nearly three weeks of quiet holiday trade but a scarcity of corporate news continued to keep many players sidelined, dealers said.
"It's been a much better day but volumes are not even close to normal," one dealer said. "But at least we are seeing some turnover."

A strangle was established B.A.T. Industries when one dealer bought 1,200 April 460 puts at 20p and at the same time bought 1,200 April 500 calls at 18p. Both options were out of the money as B.A.T shares were up 3p at 485-1/2p by 1320 GMT.
In this scenario, if B.A.T shares are priced anywhere between 460p and 500p by expiration, both options will expire worthless and the dealer will lose his entire 38p investment.
But if B.A.T shares move either above 500p or below 460p by expiration the strangle will have some value at expiration.
Elsewhere, a calendar spread was set up in ICI when one dealer sold 300 January 800 puts at 37p and then bought 300 April 800 puts at 58p.
In this case the dealer is merely attempting to capitalise on the fact that the time value premium disappears more rapidly from a near-term option than it does from the longer-term one.
The maximum profit would be established if the underlying shares were exactly at the striking price at the time of the January put expiration.
